name: Databricks Lakebase
tagline: Databricks' serverless Postgres built on Neon tech, with branching and sync to Delta tables in Unity Catalog.
description: Lakebase is Databricks' managed OLTP database: serverless PostgreSQL built on the storage and compute separation it acquired with Neon, wired into the Databricks platform. It offers autoscaling with scale-to-zero, instant copy-on-write branching, point-in-time recovery and high availability, plus synced tables that move data between Postgres and Delta Lake tables governed by Unity Catalog. That makes it a natural backend for Databricks Apps, AI agents and feature serving that need low-latency reads and writes next to lakehouse data. It reached general availability on AWS in January 2026 and on Azure in March 2026, supporting Postgres 16 to 18. Outside a Databricks estate, plain Neon is usually the simpler choice.

pricing.notes: Billed in Databricks units for compute plus storage; snapshot storage billable since June 2026; requires a Databricks workspace.

scale.notes: Autoscaling single-writer Postgres with readable secondaries; storage up to 8 TB at GA.

strengths: Postgres next to lakehouse data with managed sync to and from Delta tables
Unity Catalog governance and Databricks identity for OLTP data
Instant branching and scale-to-zero inherited from Neon
Low-latency serving layer for Databricks Apps, agents and features
weaknesses: Only usable inside a Databricks workspace
Young service; features rolling out region by region
Pricing in DBUs is harder to predict than plain per-hour billing
useCases: Backends for Databricks Apps and AI agents
Online feature and embedding serving from lakehouse pipelines
Operational stores whose data must land in Delta tables
Reverse-ETL style serving of gold tables to applications
notIdealFor: Very high write throughput needing horizontal scale
